Buttons

Five variants carrying four intents across three sizes, plus icon-only, floating and grouped forms. The set is told apart by fill: bare text, a neutral box, the accent tint for a control that is engaged, and the one accent fill for the loudest thing in a view.

Variants

Pick by emphasis. One filled button per view, at most; everything else steps down from there.

Press is a hard rule: every button gets darker when it is held down — same direction, same strength, whatever its variant and whatever its intent. Tuning that per button type is the more tempting option and it is the wrong one. “Held down” is one gesture, so it gets one answer, and nobody should have to re-learn it on the button beside the one they just learned it on. It is also the version that survives contact with a real screen: the per-type arrangement this replaced left most of the filled buttons with no visible press at all, because hover and press were the same wash of the foreground six percent apart and neither moved a saturated fill enough to see.

Hover is not the same kind of rule, and the reason is contrast rather than taste. A button with a fill of its own brightens, stepping once along its own ramp to a clean color. A button with no fill — text, icon, outlined — has nothing to brighten, so it takes a wash toward the foreground instead, which means it darkens in a light theme. Forcing those two together would make one of them invisible.

Filled
The single most important action on the screen.
Tonal
High emphasis without the weight of a solid fill.
Elevated
Needs separation from a busy or patterned background.
Outlined
A secondary action sitting beside a filled one.
Text
Low emphasis — dialog actions, card actions, inline controls.

Intents

Intent modifiers compose with any variant. Each filled intent names its own brighter hover step, the way the primary button names one; reusing the base hue as its own hover value means the button sits still under the pointer, which is indistinguishable from a button that does nothing.

Sizes

Three heights. The default is 36px; a small button suits dense toolbars and a large one suits a primary call to action.

Full width

With icons

A leading glyph clarifies the action; a trailing one signals what happens next, such as opening a menu or moving forward.

States

Hover, focus and press are handled by the shared state layer. Disabled and loading are opt-in. Use disabled for a real block; aria-disabled when the control must stay focusable.

Toolbars

A strip of controls that acts on something else on the page. The difference from a .button-group is the keyboard contract, not the border: a toolbar is one tab stop, and the arrow keys move inside it. With twelve buttons that is the difference between one press to get past the strip and twelve.

Grouped controls

Draft

Tab once to reach the strip, then the arrow keys. The item last used keeps the tab stop, so coming back lands where the work was left off rather than at the first button. A toggle carries aria-pressed, which is why it is tinted rather than filled — a filled toggle in a strip of ten reads as the page's main action.

Overflow

Narrow the window, or drag the handle at the lower-right of the box below.

Controls marked data-toolbar-overflowable are collapsed from the end until the strip fits, and the menu is built from whatever was collapsed. Undo and redo carry no such attribute, so they are never the ones to go. The rows in the menu are proxies: they click the real button, which keeps its own state and listeners.

Vertical

Canvas

A vertical strip reads top to bottom, so it takes the up and down keys instead. Direction never enters into it — only a horizontal toolbar swaps its keys in a mirrored layout.

Markup

<div class="toolbar" data-toolbar aria-label="Text formatting">
  <div class="toolbar-group">
    <button class="toolbar-button" type="button"
            data-toolbar-toggle aria-pressed="false" aria-label="Bold">
      <span class="icon">format_bold</span>
    </button>
  </div>
  <span class="toolbar-separator" role="separator"></span>

  <!-- Collapsed into the menu, last one first, when room runs out -->
  <button class="toolbar-button" type="button"
          data-toolbar-overflowable aria-label="Print">...</button>

  <div class="toolbar-overflow menu-anchor">
    <button class="toolbar-button" type="button"
            data-menu="more" aria-label="More actions">...</button>
    <div class="menu menu-end" id="more" role="menu" data-open="false"></div>
  </div>
</div>

Links

A link navigates; a button acts. Anything that changes the URL should be an anchor, even when it is styled as a button.

An inline link inside a sentence of body text.

A permanently underlined link for low-contrast surroundings.

A muted link for secondary navigation.

A link with a trailing marker arrow_forward

An anchor styled as a button

Markup

<!-- Base class plus one variant, optionally plus one intent -->
<button class="button button-filled" type="button">Label</button>
<button class="button button-outlined button-danger" type="button">Delete</button>

<!-- Icons are ligature spans; glyph-only needs a label -->
<button class="button button-filled" type="button">
  <span class="icon">add</span> Create
</button>
<button class="button button-icon" type="button" aria-label="Search">
  <span class="icon">search</span>
</button>

<!-- Toggling is wired by attribute, not by script -->
<button class="button button-icon" type="button"
        data-toggle-pressed aria-pressed="false"
        data-icon-toggle="favorite_border|favorite"
        aria-label="Like">
  <span class="icon">favorite_border</span>
</button>
